steps.title: Tithe map
steps.headline: c.1841 · Tithe map: Bute owns; John Williams occupies the holding
steps.short: About 1841: the tithe map lists Bute as owner, and John Williams as occupier.
steps.text: c.1841 · Tithe map: Bute owns; John Williams occupies the holding. VERIFIED · public copy. The tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists the Bute estate as owner and John Williams as occupier of the Great House Farm holding.
steps.say: About eighteen forty-one: the tithe map lists Bute as owner, and John Williams as occupier.

steps.title: Root title splits: A / B
steps.headline: 1877 · Root title splits: Parcel A / Parcel B
steps.short: 1877: by Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement, the title splits. Bute sells Parcel A, the farmhouse and about ten acres, to Daniel Thomas, and keeps Parcel B. When quarrying ceases, Parcel A is to be her grandfather’s.
steps.text: 1877 · Root title splits: Parcel A / Parcel B. TESTIMONY · Mary (Nancy) Williams. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement (c.1974): the Bute Estate sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas and kept about 9 acres (Parcel B). Her grandfather took a tenancy from Thomas for quarrying, and “when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather”. The 1877 instrument itself is not held (EV-0006).
steps.say: Eighteen seventy-seven: by Mary Nancy Williams's statement, the title splits. Bute sells Parcel A, the farmhouse and about ten acres, to Daniel Thomas, and keeps Parcel B. When quarrying ceases, Parcel A is to be her grandfather's.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Bute tenancy: J. Williams
steps.headline: 1916 · Bute → John Williams: yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”
steps.short: 1916: Bute grants John Williams a yearly tenancy of the whole farm, Parcel A included. It is the last tenancy of Parcel A.
steps.text: 1916 · Bute → John Williams: yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”. VERIFIED · judgment. The Court of Appeal’s history describes a February 1916 yearly agricultural tenancy of the “whole farm”. It covered Parcel A: the last tenancy of Parcel A, whose occupiers the Williams family had been since 1667. The tenancy (EV-0014) is not held.

steps.title: Bute land → Mountjoy Ltd
steps.headline: 1926 · Remaining Bute property becomes Mountjoy Ltd
steps.short: 1926: the remaining Bute property becomes Mountjoy Limited.
steps.text: 1926 · Remaining Bute property becomes Mountjoy Ltd. VERIFIED · catalogue. Archive catalogue history: after 1900 the Glamorgan estate was divided; the remaining Bute property was incorporated as Mountjoy Ltd in 1926.
steps.say: Nineteen twenty-six: the remaining Bute property becomes Mountjoy Limited.

steps.title: Last rent paid; quarry ends
steps.headline: 1928 · Last rent paid; quarrying ends: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s
steps.short: 1928: quarrying ends and the last rent is paid. By Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement, Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s.
steps.text: 1928 · Last rent paid; quarrying ends: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s. TESTIMONY · Mary (Nancy) Williams. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement (c.1974): the quarry machinery was removed in 1928 and her father made the last payment of rent, about £4 a year, to Alfred Thomas. “After this my father regarded the farm as his own.” Neither the 1877 deed nor the 1928 receipt is held.
steps.say: Nineteen twenty-eight: quarrying ends and the last rent is paid. By Mary Nancy Williams's statement, Parcel A becomes the Williams family's.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Mountjoy / Bute → WGR
steps.headline: 1938 · Mountjoy / Bute → Western Ground Rents Ltd (WGR)
steps.short: 1938: Mountjoy and Bute sell to Western Ground Rents. Which land that deed conveyed is the open question.
steps.text: 1938 · Mountjoy / Bute → Western Ground Rents Ltd (WGR). VERIFIED · deed copy + press. Sale announced 17 May 1938 and completed 23 Dec 1938. Later WGR deeds deduce title from “a Conveyance on sale dated 25th December 1938” (EV-0216, copy held). The 1938 deed and plan (EV-0019) are not held: exactly which land it conveyed is the open question.
steps.say: Nineteen thirty-eight: Mountjoy and Bute sell to Western Ground Rents. Which land that deed conveyed is the open question.

steps.title: WGR plan: Parcel B only
steps.headline: 1939 · WGR → John Williams agreement: plan shows Parcel B only
steps.short: 1939: a Western Ground Rents agreement with John Williams. Its plan shows Parcel B only.
steps.text: 1939 · WGR → John Williams agreement: plan shows Parcel B only. VERIFIED · partly held. The May 1939 WGR agreement (Glamorgan Archives DBDT123/7) is a monthly let “as meadow or pasture land”; its plan shows the eastern fields (Parcel B) only.
steps.say: Nineteen thirty-nine: a Western Ground Rents agreement with John Williams. Its plan shows Parcel B only.

steps.title: Leckwith Woods gift
steps.headline: 1940–42 · WGR gives about 109 acres of Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation
steps.short: 1940 to 42: Western Ground Rents gives Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation. No record puts Great House Farm land in that gift.
steps.text: 1940–42 · WGR gives about 109 acres of Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation. VERIFIED · secondary + press. Cardiff Parks: “The Council acquired a part of Leckwith Woods comprising some 109 acres as a gift from Western Ground Rents Ltd … offered and accepted in 1940, though the transfer of ownership was not formally completed until April 1942.” The deed carries a recreation-only covenant. The Western Mail (18 Mar 1955) reports the woods were “bought by the corporation for a nominal sum in 1942”. Not seen: the 1942 deed and plan. No record so far puts Great House Farm land in this gift; Leckwith Woods lies in Leckwith, not Llandough.
steps.say: Nineteen forty to forty-two: Western Ground Rents gives Leckwith Woods to Cardiff Corporation. No record puts Great House Farm land in that gift.

steps.title: Woodland: occupancy attempt
steps.headline: 1949 · Woodland lane: WGR’s attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation permissive, rejected
steps.short: 1949, the woodland lane: by Sion Buckler’s testimony, Mary rejects an attempt to make her occupation permissive.
steps.text: 1949 · Woodland lane: WGR’s attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation permissive, rejected. TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler · SOURCE PENDING. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026): Mary “refused a previous attempt to make her occupancy permissive in 1949, by rejecting a WGR attempt to get her into a tenancy”, and this attempt pertains to the woodland, which was registered about 12 years later in 1961 (his words; not a finding). No document of the 1949 offer or Mary’s reply is on file yet. On the record so far, WGR’s rent books show a surrender and re-grant of Frederick Buckler’s tenancy on 2 Feb 1949 with no written agreement (GHF-E122); nothing on file yet ties a 1949 offer to the woodland by plan. Earlier versions of this map placed the 1949 offer on the house. Map label: WOODLAND · REJECTED permissive occupancy ploy.
steps.say: Nineteen forty-nine, the woodland lane: by Shon Buckler's testimony, Mary rejects an attempt to make her occupation permissive.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Frederick’s farm tenancy
steps.headline: 1949–53 · Frederick Buckler’s farm tenancy (from WGR)
steps.short: 1949: Frederick Buckler’s farm tenancy from Western Ground Rents. No record shows it covered Parcel A.
steps.text: 1949–53 · Frederick Buckler’s farm tenancy (from WGR). VERIFIED · judgment. The Court of Appeal accepted a protected periodic agricultural tenancy (no written agreement). No record yet shows that it covered Parcel A; the 1939 WGR plan shows Parcel B only (EV-0023). SOURCE PENDING A reported 1954 attempt to make Frederick a tenant again (EV-0031).
steps.say: Nineteen forty-nine: Frederick Buckler's farm tenancy from Western Ground Rents. No record shows it covered Parcel A.

steps.title: Parcel B repossessed
steps.headline: 4 Jul 1955 · Possession of Parcel B, later misread and conflated with Parcel A; the woodland and the green were also seized, shortly after Mary returned from hospital with her leg amputated
steps.short: 4 July 1955: Parcel B is repossessed. The Court of Appeal records possession of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden. The woodland and green go with it; Mary stays in the house.
steps.text: 4 Jul 1955 · Possession of Parcel B, later misread and conflated with Parcel A; the woodland and the green were also seized, shortly after Mary returned from hospital with her leg amputated. TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler · VERIFIED · judgment. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026): this was the repossession of Parcel B; the order and what was done under it were later misinterpreted and conflated with Parcel A, and the woodland and the green were also seized shortly after Mary came home from hospital with her leg amputated (his words; not a finding). This station sits on Parcel B for that reason; the woodland and green have their own lanes. The Court of Appeal records that on 4 July 1955 WGR took possession of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden, so the woodland (north) and the south-east ground went with it; Mary stayed in the house. The judgment also records that Mary “had recently come out of hospital after having had a leg amputated” and was objecting very strongly to leaving the farmhouse. The order and execution return (EV-0032, EV-0034) are not held, so the exact area is unproved. SOURCE PENDING That those two areas were part of Parcel A, until the 1877 plan or the 1955 order plan is found.
steps.say: 4 July nineteen fifty-five: Parcel B is repossessed. The Court of Appeal records possession of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden. The woodland and green go with it; Mary stays in the house.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Leckwith Common inquiry
steps.headline: 1958 · Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry
steps.short: 1958: at Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry, Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler does not oppose the plan.
steps.text: 1958 · Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry. VERIFIED · press. The Western Mail (7 May 1958) reports Cardiff City Council’s plan to turn Leckwith Common into a playing field. Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler of Great House Farm said she did not oppose it, and that about 130 years earlier Lord Bute had allowed her family “a slice of land” which was now Leckwith Common.
steps.say: Nineteen fifty-eight: at Cardiff City Council's Leckwith Common inquiry, Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler does not oppose the plan.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Green: occupancy attempt
steps.headline: 1958/9 · Green lane: attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation permissive, refused
steps.short: 1958 to 59, the green lane: Mary refuses a tenancy offered by Western Ground Rents. By Sion Buckler’s testimony, this attempt concerns the green.
steps.text: 1958/9 · Green lane: attempt to make Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation permissive, refused. TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler · VERIFIED · judgment. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026): the 1958/9 permissive occupancy attempt belongs to the green, south of the house and garden and now Church View Close park, and it led to the 1970 registration of the green (his words; not a finding). The record held: the Court of Appeal’s history records that in 1959 WGR offered Mary a tenancy and she refused it; the judgment describes that offer as a tenancy of the house and garden, and no plan ties it to the green. The offer and reply are not held. Map label: GREEN · REJECTED permissive occupancy ploy.
steps.say: Nineteen fifty-eight to fifty-nine, the green lane: Mary refuses a tenancy offered by Western Ground Rents. By Shon Buckler's testimony, this attempt concerns the green.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: Woodland registration
steps.headline: 1961 · Woodland lane: registration of the woodland, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt (Sion Buckler)
steps.short: 1961, the woodland lane: a deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick and Tile, and Cardiff City Corporation. By Sion Buckler’s testimony, the woodland is registered, twelve years after 1949.
steps.text: 1961 · Woodland lane: registration of the woodland, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt (Sion Buckler). TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler · SOURCE PENDING · VERIFIED · register held. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026): the woodland was registered in 1961, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt (his words; not a finding). No 1961 registration document is on file yet. The record held: the woodland register WA735527 (copy held) lists “a Deed dated 29 March 1961 made between (1) Western Ground Rents Limited (2) The South Western Brick & Tile Company Limited and (3) Cardiff City Corporation”; the land tinted pink is subject to the rights in it, and the register notes “Copy filed under WA231076”. The deed and its plan have not been inspected. The 1994 transfer is a separate, later event on this lane. Map label: WOODLAND · usual 12-year waiting period · measured: about 12 yrs (1949 → 1961); WOODLAND · clandestine registration · source pending.
steps.say: Nineteen sixty-one, the woodland lane: a deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick and Tile, and Cardiff City Corporation. By Shon Buckler's testimony, the woodland is registered, twelve years after nineteen forty-nine.

steps.title: Possession order
steps.headline: 11 Dec 1962 · Possession order: farmhouse and garden. The BP house lane starts here
steps.short: 11 December 1962: a county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden. It is not enforced before 1974.
steps.text: 11 Dec 1962 · Possession order: farmhouse and garden. The BP house lane starts here. UNVERIFIED. Cardiff County Court order as recorded on the wiki; the original order and plan are not held. The order was never enforced before 1974 (1962 Possession Order page). Sion Buckler calls it unenforced and “arguably legally unenforceable” (his words; not a finding).
steps.say: 11 December nineteen sixty-two: a county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden. It is not enforced before nineteen seventy-four.

steps.title: Weekly tenancy offer
steps.headline: 1965 · Further weekly tenancy offer; not signed, no rent paid
steps.short: 1965: Mrs Buckler is offered a weekly tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid. Sion Buckler calls this the second ploy.
steps.text: 1965 · Further weekly tenancy offer; not signed, no rent paid. VERIFIED · judgment. Recorded in the Court of Appeal’s history: in March 1965 WGR’s agents offered Mrs Buckler a tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid. Sion Buckler calls this the second “ploy” (his words; not a finding).
steps.say: Nineteen sixty-five: Mrs Buckler is offered a weekly tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid. Shon Buckler calls this the second ploy.

steps.title: Lands Tribunal v Cardiff
steps.headline: 1967 · Lands Tribunal: WGR v City of Cardiff
steps.short: 1967: Western Ground Rents and the City of Cardiff go to the Lands Tribunal. Which land it concerned has not been read.
steps.text: 1967 · Lands Tribunal: WGR v City of Cardiff. VERIFIED · catalogue only. A compulsory-purchase compensation case, catalogued at The National Archives. Which land it concerned has not been read.
steps.say: Nineteen sixty-seven: Western Ground Rents and the City of Cardiff go to the Lands Tribunal. Which land it concerned has not been read.

steps.title: BP acquires
steps.headline: 31 Dec 1969 · WGR → BP Pension Trust: BP takes WGR’s interest, including the 1962 order
steps.short: 31 December 1969: BP Pension Trust takes Western Ground Rents’ interest: Parcel B, and the 1962 order.
steps.text: 31 Dec 1969 · WGR → BP Pension Trust: BP takes WGR’s interest, including the 1962 order. VERIFIED · judgment. Conveyance recited as the root of BP’s title. The instrument and plan (EV-0043) are not held. The same conveyance carried Parcel B, so the station shows on both lines. In September 1974 BP applied for leave to enforce the 1962 order, so it held that order’s benefit. Sion Buckler: “BP’s 1969 acquisition of the interest in the unenforced and arguably legally unenforceable 1962 possession order” (his words).
steps.say: 31 December nineteen sixty-nine: B P Pension Trust takes Western Ground Rents' interest: Parcel B, and the nineteen sixty-two order.

steps.title: Village green VG41
steps.headline: 16 Jun 1970 · South-east ground registered as village green VG41 · about 11–12 yrs after the 1958/9 attempt
steps.short: 16 June 1970: the green is registered as village green VG41, about twelve years after the 1958 attempt.
steps.text: 16 Jun 1970 · South-east ground registered as village green VG41 · about 11–12 yrs after the 1958/9 attempt. UNVERIFIED. The date as recorded on the wiki. The application, map and ownership section of the VG41 file are not held; registration as a green does not by itself show who owns it. Llandough Community Council states that it “owns and maintains the village green”. Sion Buckler calls this a “clandestine” registration of part of Parcel A (his words; not a finding). Map label: GREEN · usual 12-year waiting period · measured: about 11–12 yrs (1958/9 → 16 Jun 1970); GREEN · clandestine registration · source pending.
steps.say: 16 June nineteen seventy: the green is registered as village green V G forty-one, about twelve years after the nineteen fifty-eight attempt.

steps.title: Ordnance Survey altered
steps.headline: 1971 · BP house lane: Ordnance Survey alteration
steps.short: 1971: Sion Buckler describes an alteration of the Ordnance Survey. No record of it is on the wiki yet.
steps.text: 1971 · BP house lane: Ordnance Survey alteration. TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler · SOURCE PENDING. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026) describes “some corruption of the Ordnance Survey in 1971” (his words; “corruption” is his word, not a finding). No 1971 Ordnance Survey sheet, revision record or correspondence is on the wiki yet. The one 1971 record known on this lane is BP Pension Trust’s 1971 abstract of title, known only from later recitals and not held (EV-0045).
steps.say: Nineteen seventy-one: Shon Buckler describes an alteration of the Ordnance Survey. No record of it is on the wiki yet.

steps.title: Attempt to extinguish fails
steps.headline: 1974 · BP house lane: BP’s attempt to extinguish Mary (Nancy) Williams’s ownership claim fails
steps.short: 1974: Mary opens the farmhouse to the public: “my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it.” BP’s possession action is adjourned, and never listed again. Its attempt to extinguish her ownership claim fails.
steps.text: 1974 · BP house lane: BP’s attempt to extinguish Mary (Nancy) Williams’s ownership claim fails. VERIFIED · press · UNVERIFIED · court papers. On 15 April 1974 Mary opened the farmhouse to the public and said: “my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it” (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974). BP brought a fresh county-court action for possession; on 3 July 1974 Mary pleaded that she owned the house parcel and relied on the Limitation Act 1939. The hearing was part-heard and adjourned, and was never listed again. BP also obtained leave on 19 Sep 1974 to enforce the 1962 order; Mary’s solicitors appealed because she had not been given notice, and the warrant was withdrawn on 31 Oct 1974. The court papers are not held (EV-0049). Sion Buckler calls this a failed attempt to extinguish her ownership claim (his words).
steps.say: Nineteen seventy-four: Mary opens the farmhouse to the public: "my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it." B P's possession action is adjourned, and never listed again. Its attempt to extinguish her ownership claim fails.

img.cap: Mary (Nancy) Williams, formerly Buckler, at Tŷ Mawr. Family photograph.

steps.title: BP licence letters
steps.headline: 31 Oct 1974 · BP letters offer continued rent-free occupation of the house
steps.short: 31 October 1974: BP’s letters offer her rent-free occupation of the house. She never expressly accepts or rejects them. Sion Buckler calls this the third ploy.
steps.text: 31 Oct 1974 · BP letters offer continued rent-free occupation of the house. VERIFIED · judgment. The letters were one-sided: the judgment records that Mrs Buckler “never expressly accepted or rejected the terms of the two letters”. In July 1974 her defence had asserted that the claim was barred by adverse possession. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse” (Dillon LJ). Sion Buckler calls this the third “ploy” (his words; not a finding). Map label: BP HOUSE · REJECTED permissive occupancy ploy.
steps.say: 31 October nineteen seventy-four: B P's letters offer her rent-free occupation of the house. She never expressly accepts or rejects them. Shon Buckler calls this the third ploy.

steps.text: 30 Nov 1982 · BP Properties Ltd applies to register WA231076 (the farm). VERIFIED · HMLR. Application date from HM Land Registry’s file schedule (30 items).

steps.title: BP applies: house

steps.text: 2 Feb 1987 · WA240304 merged into WA231076: the house branch joins Parcel B. VERIFIED · HMLR. Amalgamation recorded during the appeal; the application and plan (EV-0078) are not held. Sion Buckler’s reading: the BP house title was merged into Parcel B “as if it were Mary’s Parcel A” (his words).

steps.title: Court of Appeal
steps.headline: 31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2
steps.short: 31 July 1987: the Court of Appeal decides the farmhouse and garden only, and holds that the letters made her possession a licence. From here, no register shows the Williams title to Parcel A.
steps.text: 31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2. VERIFIED · judgment. The appeal concerned the farmhouse and garden only. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse”, so the adverse-possession claim to the farmhouse and garden failed. From here no register shows the Williams Parcel A title; the line runs on unregistered. Sion Buckler’s words for this: “buried alive” (see his testimony).
steps.say: 31 July nineteen eighty-seven: the Court of Appeal decides the farmhouse and garden only, and holds that the letters made her possession a licence. From here, no register shows the Williams title to Parcel A.

steps.title: Eviction, demolition
steps.headline: Nov–Dec 1988 · Eviction, then demolition (6 Dec 1988)
steps.short: November 1988: possession is enforced. On 6 December, BP demolishes the farmhouse.
steps.text: Nov–Dec 1988 · Eviction, then demolition (6 Dec 1988). VERIFIED · press. Possession was enforced at the end of November 1988 (forced entry reported for 30 Nov). BP demolished the farmhouse in the early hours of 6 December 1988.
steps.say: November nineteen eighty-eight: possession is enforced. On 6 December, B P demolishes the farmhouse.

steps.title: Outline planning
steps.headline: 1989–90 · Planning 89/01396/OUT: Cardiff Bay Development Corporation consulted
steps.short: 1989: outline planning. Cardiff Bay Development Corporation is consulted, not Cardiff City Council.
steps.text: 1989–90 · Planning 89/01396/OUT: Cardiff Bay Development Corporation consulted. VERIFIED · scan read. BP Properties’ outline application (received 8 Nov 1989; granted 13 Mar 1990). The planning officer’s report lists among the consultees: “Cardiff Bay Development Corporation: No objections – however, the Corporation would hope that the trees on the slope of the site facing north-west are retained and that the public right of way which runs through the site will be retained.” This is Cardiff Bay Development Corporation, not Cardiff City Council. The full response is outstanding; Sion Buckler requested it from the Vale on 18 Sep 2026.
steps.say: Nineteen eighty-nine: outline planning. Cardiff Bay Development Corporation is consulted, not Cardiff City Council.

steps.text: 1992 · Reserved matters 92/00671/RES: 20 houses; no Cardiff body named. VERIFIED · scan read. Ideal Homes Wales’ Form D (14 May 1992) names no Cardiff City or Cardiff Bay body. steps.title: BP → Ideal Homes
steps.headline: 3 Dec 1993 · BP → Ideal Homes (farm site and woodland)
steps.short: 3 December 1993: BP to Ideal Homes, the farm site and woodland; the deed is not seen. The houses become Church View Close.
steps.text: 3 Dec 1993 · BP → Ideal Homes (farm site and woodland). UNVERIFIED. Recorded in the woodland title history on the wiki; the houses became Church View Close. Forest of Cardiff states that it bought the woodland from Ideal Homes (now Persimmon) “after due diligence”. Deed not seen.
steps.say: 3 December nineteen ninety-three: B P to Ideal Homes, the farm site and woodland; the deed is not seen. The houses become Church View Close.

steps.title: Change of hands
steps.headline: 10 Nov 1994 · Woodland changes hands: transfer to Forest of Cardiff, title WA735527 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation), not the 1961 registration
steps.short: 10 November 1994: the woodland passes to Forest of Cardiff, a separate event from 1961.
steps.text: 10 Nov 1994 · Woodland changes hands: transfer to Forest of Cardiff, title WA735527 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation), not the 1961 registration. VERIFIED · register held. Transfer with plan to Forest of Cardiff, registered as WA735527. The current register copy is held (EV-0169); the 1994 transfer itself (EV-0136) is not. Forest of Cardiff’s accounts to 31 Mar 1995 show no land as an asset. The register (B1) enters Forest of Cardiff as proprietor on 25 Nov 1994. It recites a 23 May 1975 conveyance of part (“the land tinted blue … and other land”) from The British Petroleum Pension Trust to B.P. Properties Ltd, and notes copies of earlier deeds as “filed under WA231076”. Sion Buckler: in 1994 the woodland “changed hands again” (his words; not a finding). It is a separate event from the 1961 registration. Map label: WOODLAND · change of hands / new proprietor · not the 1961 registration.
steps.say: 10 November nineteen ninety-four: the woodland passes to Forest of Cardiff, a separate event from nineteen sixty-one.

steps.title: WA735527 part sold
steps.headline: 2005–06 · Part of WA735527 sold to Goldsworthy Homes: £20,000 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation)
steps.short: 2005: part of the woodland title is sold to Goldsworthy Homes.
steps.text: 2005–06 · Part of WA735527 sold to Goldsworthy Homes: £20,000 · change of hands / new proprietor (or further synthetic-parcel creation). VERIFIED · Companies House. A 2005 transfer excised land from WA735527 (EV-0139, not held); register entry A4 dated 22 Dec 2005 records the excised land being registered under a new title. Forest of Cardiff’s audited accounts to 30 Jun 2006 record “Sale of Land – Leckwith Road, Llandough £20,000”.
steps.say: Two thousand and five: part of the woodland title is sold to Goldsworthy Homes.

steps.title: Where each line stands
steps.headline: 2026 · Where each line stands today
steps.short: Today: Church View Close stands on the merged title. The woodland is Forest of Cardiff’s; the green is village green VG41. Parcel A’s Williams line runs on, unregistered.
steps.text: 2026 · Where each line stands today. VERIFIED · registers. Merged title WA231076 (house third + Parcel B): built over as Church View Close. Forest third: Forest of Cardiff, WA735527. Green third: village green VG41. Parcel A: the Williams line runs on, unregistered. HM Land Registry copies of the 1982–83 files are on order.
steps.say: Today: Church View Close stands on the merged title. The woodland is Forest of Cardiff's; the green is village green V G forty-one. Parcel A's Williams line runs on, unregistered.

steps.title: Parcel A: Williams title
steps.headline: 2026 · Parcel A: Williams title, not extinguished and not sold (Sion Buckler; no deed of sale on file)
steps.short: No deed of sale by Mary (Nancy) Williams is on file, and the 1987 appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. By Sion Buckler’s testimony, the Williams title to Parcel A is not extinguished, and not sold.
steps.text: 2026 · Parcel A: Williams title, not extinguished and not sold (Sion Buckler; no deed of sale on file). TESTIMONY · Sion Buckler. No deed of sale by Mary (Nancy) Williams is on file, and the 1987 appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. Since 1987 no register has shown the Williams Parcel A title, about 38 years, while the three branch titles have been treated as valid. Sion Buckler (19 Oct 2026): “Our title fades but remains. Not exstiguished or sold.” SOURCE PENDING A sale c.1965 reported in a cousin’s written account (held privately) is unidentified.
steps.say: No deed of sale by Mary Nancy Williams is on file, and the nineteen eighty-seven appeal decided the farmhouse and garden only. By Shon Buckler's testimony, the Williams title to Parcel A is not extinguished, and not sold.

parcelA.label: Parcel A
parcelA.note: Dotted outline: the whole of Parcel A from the 1877 split (Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement), kept on every later step. The woodland, green and house-and-yard labels appear at the step that first discusses each; the green is drawn as the lower third of Parcel A.

opening: This is the story of the true owners of Church View Close, Llandough, and why people incorrectly think it's Cardiff Forest, BP and Llandough Council.
framing: Station by station, it follows the title-chain map on the Legal Wiki’s home page, and shows why the Williams family’s title to Parcel A was never extinguished.
closing: Three attempts to make Mary’s occupation look permissive were rejected. Each was followed by a registration of part of Parcel A in another name. And the Williams title to Parcel A was never extinguished: the line runs on.
